tasks.task: Turn course material into revision notes

items.when: When a learner has lecture notes, slides or chapters that are too long to revise from
When the source is messy and needs tidy nested bullets before anything else
When a chapter is dense, to map its claims and evidence before you shorten it
When one idea is clearer as a diagram or table placed beside the words
When you need to ask the learner's own files where a point comes from before you keep it

tasks.task: Make a one-page summary, formula sheet or glossary

items.when: When the notes exist and the learner wants one page of key terms and formulas for a topic
When a glossary is needed, to sort the words into everyday, course and subject terms
When two terms keep getting mixed up and need side-by-side examples
When the sheet has formulas or worked numbers, to check units and rounding
When you want to try the page as a diagram or table and compare it with bullets

tasks.task: Build a revision timetable to the exam date

items.when: When there is a fixed exam date and a pile of material, to order the work from now to exam day
When the notes are done and you need the day-by-day plan that goes with them
When you have the syllabus or past papers and must rank what to study first
When topics and dates are known and each topic must come back at widening gaps
When the learner has few hours, to compare plans and pick one they will keep
When the plan does one topic per block, to mix related topics for stronger recall
When the plan is long cramming blocks and should fit the learner's real week

tasks.task: Build a flashcard deck from the learner's notes

items.when: When you need one-fact cards, cloze cards or vocabulary cards as a file that imports cleanly
When you want a quick second set of question-and-answer cards to compare wording
When the learner has no card app and needs a recall session with next review dates
When cards ask the learner to recognise an answer and should make them recall it
After building a deck, to catch two-fact cards, duplicates and answers that disagree with the notes

tasks.task: Check and clean up an existing deck

items.when: When an Anki or Quizlet deck has two-fact cards, wrong answers, duplicates or import errors
When bad cards must be rewritten to one fact each and tagged by chapter

tasks.task: Write self-test questions with answers

items.when: When you have lesson notes and need a short recall quiz at three levels, with answers
When the learner can recite a fact but cannot say why it is true
When the learner feels ready, to test them with hard questions and mark each answer
Before the learner sits it, to check the questions test the stated goals and mark fairly
When every question is "what is" and you want a set that asks why and how

tasks.task: Build a full practice exam with explanations

items.when: When you have the study guide and exam outline and need a weighted exam with reasons
When the exam is one step in the run to exam day and must be timed with the plan
When a domain needs extra problems that rise in difficulty and vary just enough
When answers are calculations, to check units and that the key is right
Before release, to check each question tests the outline and has one best answer
When questions test trivia and should test what the learner must think about

tasks.task: Write scenario questions and a question bank by topic

items.when: When the exam uses scenarios and each question must trace to the study guide
When the learner passes plain questions and needs new cases that test the same rule
When a common mistake should be built into an example for the learner to find
Before the bank is used, to find questions with two right answers or unfair wording

tasks.task: Turn practice scores into a study plan

items.when: When a learner has taken a practice exam and has a fixed exam date
When you have the wrong answers and need the likely cause behind each kind
When the same errors repeat and need targeted practice and a later recall check
At each review, to compare progress with the plan and adjust the practice

tasks.task: Help a stuck learner without giving the answer

items.when: When a learner is stuck on a practice problem and asks for the answer
Before any hint, to work out why they are stuck so the help aims at the real gap
When a problem type comes up often and needs a set of hints from nudge to full step
When you have the learner's work and need a diagnosis, hints and easier tasks to climb
When hints stall, to try having the learner explain what they tried and build on that
After they solve it, to have them teach the step back and show it has stuck

tasks.task: Explain a hard idea so it sticks

items.when: Before explaining, to see the usual mistakes on this topic and the examples that clear them
When the learner knows another field and an everyday analogy with its limits would help
When a mechanism is best shown with the smallest example that works, traced step by step
When you want the learner to explain first and then build on what they said
After explaining, to have the learner teach it back and see the gaps
When the explanation leans on jargon and should use plain words and a real example

tasks.task: Move a learner from worked examples to solving alone

items.when: When a procedure needs a run from fully worked examples to solving alone
When you have one good example and need staged problems that take the help away
When the learner follows examples but freezes alone, to plan the path between
When they are ready for a mixed set that gets harder a little at a time
When you want practice built on finding a planted mistake, as a change from solving
Before taking the help away, to ask one question that shows they follow the method

tasks.task: Check a request before helping with marked work

items.when: When a learner asks for help with an essay, coursework, take-home test or project
When you need to say which parts of an assignment help is fair for and which it would ruin

tasks.task: Give feedback on a draft without writing it

items.when: Before reading the draft, to confirm what help the course allows
When you have the draft and the criteria and need what is missing and why
When the learner cannot structure an argument and needs a frame to fill in themselves
Before you send feedback, to check it is specific and leaves the work to the learner

tasks.task: Write a language practice set for one topic and level

items.when: When you need words, a dialogue, drills and a speaking task for one topic at one level
Each week, to prepare fresh practice for the lesson and short practice between classes
When learners need sentence starters at two or three levels to get speaking
When the language is Spanish or Turkish and a learner's paragraph needs corrections and drills
When the set is drafted, to find words and sentence types above the stated level

tasks.task: Write role-play and conversation cards

items.when: When a class needs speaking practice for a real situation with a goal for each person
When the cards must reuse the words and phrases from this week's practice set
When weaker speakers need starter phrases printed on their card
Before class, to find words and sentence types on the cards that are above the level

tasks.task: Make vocabulary decks and listening practice

items.when: When a word list must become two-way vocabulary cards with example sentences
When a text has too many new words, to choose which are worth a card
When learners need to hear the dialogue, with a checked script and a text to follow
When you need the dialogue spoken in a natural voice for listening practice
Before the deck is shared, to catch duplicate words and cards that test two things

tasks.task: Check a learner's level or progress

items.when: When a new learner starts a topic and you need a quick level check before lessons
When one question should show who has the point and who needs more help
When a learner is over- or under-confident, to compare how sure they felt with how they did

tasks.task: Set up daily practice by text or email

items.when: When learners need a few minutes of practice each day between classes
When each day's message should bring back earlier words at the right gap
When each message needs two or three recall questions with answers the next day
Before the messages are set up, to check each one is short and at the learner's reading level

tasks.task: Plan a tutoring session on one topic

items.when: When you know the topic and learner and need an explanation, practice and a quiz
When a skill is new and should go from you showing it to them doing it alone
Before the session, to cut overload and add checks of understanding
After the session, to update the learner's profile and note where to resume

tasks.task: Coach study methods and habits

items.when: When a learner rereads and highlights, to choose methods that fit the material and goal
When the learner should write what they remember first and only then fill the gaps
When a learner plans to revise and does not, to set if-then plans and an obstacle check
When a method feels good now but does not show up in results a week later
When a learner says they are just bad at it and needs a next strategy

tasks.task: Adapt material for a learner's needs or English level

items.when: When a learner has an access need and the same material must work for them
When one task needs changing for one learner with the goal kept the same
When the learner is still learning English and needs language help without easier thinking
When an English learner needs a task that still asks for real thinking
Before you hand it over, to check the text is not harder than the learner can read
When you want several ways to present the content and let the learner show what they know

tasks.task: Guide a learner through a hard text or paper

items.when: When a set text is hard, to choose the reading strategies that fit its hard parts
When the text is a research paper and they need its main idea and what to read closely
When they must take notes on an article or chapter: claims, evidence and gaps
After reading, to test recall of the claims and evidence

always.when: Before any notes, deck or exam goes to the learner, to catch typos and terms spelt two ways
Whenever the work might be marked, to stay on the right side of what help is fair

helpers.when: When a school or provider needs a whole course or scheme of work, not practice for one learner
When practice must become an online course with modules and tracking
When materials or parent messages must be in a second language and checked by a specialist
When a learner's own finished writing needs a proofread within what their course allows
When the goal is a job interview or career move, not an exam

gaps: No library item builds Anki or Quizlet decks or cloze cards; only the kit skill does
No library item checks an existing flashcard deck for two-fact cards, duplicates or wrong answers
No library item builds a certification practice exam weighted by domain with a reason for every answer
No library item writes multiple-choice questions with wrong options built from common mistakes
No library item checks revision notes or answers against the learner's own course material
No library item writes language drills, dialogues or role-play cards by CEFR level
No library item runs a language placement or progress check
No library item covers pronunciation or speaking feedback
No library item writes daily practice messages by text or email
No library item writes a progress report for a parent or a training provider
No library item covers exam technique: timing, command words and what to do on the day
No library item covers safeguarding and children's data for tutors who work with under-18s
No library item gives clearly different versions of revision notes, practice sets, role-play cards or exam questions to compare
No library item checks a language practice set for wrong answers or unnatural phrases in the target language
